name: Protein Extraction
description: Total protein extraction from mammalian cells using RIPA lysis buffer. Suitable for Western blot, ELISA, co-IP, and other protein assays. Fresh protease inhibitors are essential.
source_note: General educational template for RIPA-buffer-based total protein extraction.

steps.title: Prepare RIPA lysis buffer with inhibitors
steps.description: Prepare ice-cold RIPA buffer supplemented with fresh protease inhibitor cocktail (and phosphatase inhibitors if studying signaling). Calculate volume based on number of samples.
steps.notes: Prepare fresh on the day of experiment. Keep on ice throughout.

steps.title: Remove media and wash cells with ice-cold PBS
steps.description: Aspirate cell culture media. Wash cells 2–3 times with ice-cold PBS to remove serum proteins and debris. Aspirate last PBS wash completely.
steps.notes: Working quickly on ice slows proteolysis. Complete removal of PBS prevents sample dilution.

steps.title: Add RIPA buffer and lyse cells
steps.description: Add pre-prepared RIPA buffer directly to cells. Scrape cells from dish using a cell scraper. Transfer lysate to a chilled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
steps.notes: Typical volumes: 100–200 µL for 6-well plate; 500 µL for 10 cm dish. Incubate 20–30 min on ice for complete lysis.
steps.warnings: RIPA contains detergents — avoid foaming. Wear gloves.

steps.title: Centrifuge to clear lysate
steps.description: Centrifuge at maximum speed to pellet cell debris, nuclei, and insoluble material. Transfer the clear supernatant (total cell lysate) to a fresh chilled tube.
steps.notes: Avoid lipid layer on surface of supernatant — aspirate carefully from the middle. Pellet contains insoluble cytoskeletal proteins and nuclear debris.

steps.title: Protein quantification
steps.description: Measure protein concentration of each cleared lysate using BCA or Bradford assay. Use known BSA standards for the standard curve. Run samples in duplicate.
steps.notes: Typical lysate concentrations: 1–10 µg/µL. Dilute samples if concentration is very high.
steps.warnings: Bradford reagent stains clothes and skin. Coomassie-based reagents are used in Bradford assay.

steps.title: Aliquot and store protein lysates
steps.description: Aliquot lysates into small volumes to avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles. Label tubes with sample ID, concentration, and date. Store at −80°C for long-term storage or use immediately.
steps.notes: At −80°C, protein lysates are stable for months to years. At −20°C, stable for several weeks. Avoid >3 freeze-thaw cycles.
